RlsGuardRunner.run_sql calls _refuse_denied_functions (safety/__init__.py:196-197), which raises UnsafeSqlError on every path (208-219), before the inner runner, so no rows are returned. RunSqlTool.execute (agent/tools/run_sql.py:57-61) awaits self.sql_runner.run_sql inside a try whose `except Exception` (182-197) returns ToolResult(success=False, error=str(e), metadata error_type sql_error), the same handling as the read-only guard's UnsafeSqlError (raised the same way at safety/__init__.py:100). query_database.py:497-504 also has an `except UnsafeSqlError` branch that re-raises it as RuntimeError(str(e)) (documented there as a defensive path). A denylist refusal therefore comes back as a structured error result, not a crash and not rows. The rejection line about the MySQL routine-lookup test is unrelated to this claim.

apply_rls ends with tree.sql(dialect=dialect) (rls.py:332); values are built as literal nodes. sqlglot generator sets _escaped_quote_end = tokenizer STRING_ESCAPES[0] + QUOTE_END (generator.py:969); MySQL Tokenizer.STRING_ESCAPES = ["'", '"', '\\'] (dialects/mysql.py:86), so the first is "'" and a single quote is emitted as '' (doubled), never \'. escape_str (generator.py:3216-3229) first maps backslash to a doubled backslash via ESCAPED_SEQUENCES (MySQL supports escape sequences since '\\' is in STRING_ESCAPES), then doubles quotes. So value \' becomes \\'' . _mysql_parse_sql (readonly.py:487-503) consumes backslash+non-quote as a 2-char pair (i+=2), treats doubled quotes as an escaped quote, and only raises when backslash is immediately followed by the quote char (line 492-493). The generated forms (\\ pairs, '' doubles, \n/\0 style sequences) never present backslash-then-quote at a token boundary, so the check does not refuse them. RlsGuardRunner calls assert_no_denied_functions on the rewritten SQL (safety/__init__.py:197,207) which goes through _parse_statements -> _mysql_parse_sql (readonly.py:546-549). Checked against sqlglot in repo .venv (version may differ from head pin, not verified). The rejection line is about an unrelated test and does not cover this item.

readonly.py:575-577 loops over _parse_statements(sql, dialect) (sqlglot.parse at line 549) and raises UnsafeSqlError('empty parse tree') for any None entry. RlsGuardRunner (safety/__init__.py:197,207) passes it the `rewritten` string, which apply_rls returns as tree.sql(dialect=dialect) (rls.py:332), so it is generator output with no trailing semicolon. Even with a trailing semicolon, sqlglot Parser._parse (installed sqlglot parser.py:2326-2331) only starts a new chunk `if i < total - 1`, so a trailing ';' adds no empty chunk and no None entry. None arises only from an empty chunk such as 'SELECT 1;;', which a single rewritten statement does not produce. Rejection line concerns an unrelated test, so it does not cover this item.

Traced sqlglot tokenizer_core.py (_scan_keywords 826-885, _scan_var 1145-1161, _scan_number 959-1038). Multi-word/keyword matches add text=word.upper() that is in KEYWORDS; _scan_var yields VAR or keywords.get(text.upper()); quoted names are IDENTIFIER. So for ordinary names (bare, qualified, quoted, backticked) the claim holds. Counterexample to the literal claim: MySQL name like `1e(`. _scan_number consumes '1', then 'e' as a scientific marker (scientific=1), then peek '(' hits the else/break; it emits NUMBER '1e' (line 1034), not VAR (the identifiers_can_start_with_digit VAR path at 1020-1021 is only reached when an identifier char follows). Token type NUMBER and '1E' not in KEYWORDS, so relations.py:101-103 would skip it. MySQL itself lexes '1e' without exponent digits as an identifier, so a stored function so named could be called unnoticed. However, no unchanged requirement text in both views demands this property (base docs/internal/database-connectors/row-level-security.md:45 says stored functions were an uninspected gap; the call check is added by the PR), so no FAIL requirement can be quoted; the claim is not shown correct either, so INCONCLUSIVE. I did not execute the tokenizer (no shell available); the trace is by reading.

sqlglot Tokenizer._scan_identifier (sqlglot/tokenizer_core.py:1138-1143) calls self._advance() to step past the opening quote, then _extract_string(identifier_end, ...) reads up to the closing quote, and adds IDENTIFIER with that text. The stored token text therefore has no quote characters. _called_names (src/sqllens/safety/relations.py:98-106) uses token.text for IDENTIFIER tokens followed by L_PAREN, so "ALL_ORDERS" (postgres) and `ALL_ORDERS` (mysql, whose IDENTIFIERS include the backtick) yield the bare name ALL_ORDERS. Checked in the main-repo venv's sqlglot; the installed version in the review environment was not separately checked.

relations.py:104-106 adds text, text.lower() and an ASCII-only lowercase (non-ASCII chars unchanged) to the set, matching the docstring at 90-92. PostgreSQL downcase_identifier (scansup.c) lowercases ASCII A-Z always, but folds high-bit characters only when the database encoding is single-byte (and isupper per locale); in multibyte encodings such as UTF8 it leaves them alone. So the rationale that non-ASCII folding depends on server encoding is accurate, and returning both full-lower and ASCII-lower covers both cases. The rejections line concerns an unrelated test and does not cover this item.

relations.py:247-255 executes the pg_proc query with '= ANY(%s)' twice and params (names, names), where names is a Python list of str. The list is never empty at that point: relations.py:126 returns early when both relations and called are empty, and :132 calls _refuse_database_routines only when `called` is non-empty. PostgresRunner (postgres/sql_runner.py:140-142,169) opens a psycopg2 connection and passes that conn to verify_base_tables. relations.py:128 uses connection.cursor(), a plain psycopg2 cursor with %s paramstyle. psycopg2 adapts a list of str to ARRAY['a','b'], which Postgres resolves to text[]. Both comparisons are text = ANY(text[]), because proname::text is cast to text. I did not run it against a live database. The conclusion rests on psycopg2's documented list adaptation and the code read.

relations.py:247-255 runs SELECT p.proname FROM pg_catalog.pg_proc p JOIN pg_catalog.pg_namespace n ON n.oid = p.pronamespace WHERE n.nspname NOT IN ('pg_catalog','information_schema') AND (p.proname::text = ANY(names) OR lower(p.proname::text) = ANY(names)) LIMIT 1. These are the real pg_proc/pg_namespace columns. There is no filter on arguments or extension, so every row outside the two schemas matches (extension routines are ordinary pg_proc rows in non-pg_catalog schemas), across all signatures. _called_names (84-107) supplies each called name as written, lower-cased and ASCII-lower-cased. A call to MYFUNC against a routine created as "MyFunc" therefore matches through lower(proname), and an exact quoted call matches through proname. Matching is case-insensitive as claimed. The rejection line concerns the MySQL test fake and is not this claim.

relations.py:256-263 MySQL arm runs 'SELECT ROUTINE_NAME FROM information_schema.ROUTINES WHERE ROUTINE_TYPE = 'FUNCTION' AND LOWER(ROUTINE_NAME) IN (%s,...) LIMIT 1' with tuple(names), matching the claim (pymysql %s paramstyle, tuple args). No schema filter, so any schema is matched. Case: names come from _called_names (lines 97-107) which adds text, text.lower() and an ASCII-lowercase variant, so LOWER(ROUTINE_NAME) matches the lowercase form regardless of case (MySQL LOWER also folds non-ASCII, covered by text.lower()). ROUTINES lists only routines the user may access/execute, which are the only ones callable, so visibility does not undermine the claim. The rejection line (test fake can't observe the column) concerns a different subject and is not needed.

relations.py:84-107 _called_names tokenizes the executed SQL (callers pass args.sql unchanged: postgres sql_runner.py:169, mysql sql_runner.py:138) and collects any VAR/IDENTIFIER/keyword token followed by L_PAREN, so a built-in written as strpos( is collected by name regardless of sqlglot's typed rename. _refuse_database_routines (238-270) matches only on name: postgres pg_proc with nspname NOT IN (pg_catalog, information_schema), no pronamespace/argument filter beyond name, and a lowercase-folded compare; mysql LOWER(ROUTINE_NAME) IN names. No argument-signature or schema condition, so a user routine sharing the built-in's written name (any schema outside the system ones, any signature) triggers RlsError (266-270). Adversarial input traced: user function public.strpos(int) and query calling strpos('a','b') -> name 'strpos' collected and matched -> refused. A built-in written differently (POSITION(... IN ...), or CURRENT_DATE with no paren) yields a different token/name and is not a call by that name, consistent with 'shares its name' as written. Docstring matches the code. The rejection line concerns a MySQL test and is not relevant.

relations.py:123-135: verify_base_tables computes `called` for postgres/mysql independent of `relations`; it returns early only when both are empty, and calls _refuse_database_routines whenever `called` is non-empty, so the 'whether or not a relation is referenced' clause holds. If _relations raises RlsError first (line 124), the statement is refused anyway, so a call reached only through such a statement is still refused. _called_names (84-107) emits text, text.lower() and an ASCII-only lower for each VAR/IDENTIFIER/keyword token before '('. The PostgreSQL query (248-255) matches proname = ANY(names) OR lower(proname) = ANY(names) outside pg_catalog/information_schema. Non-ASCII trace: a call written with uppercase non-ASCII letters yields the ASCII-folded form PostgreSQL uses in a UTF8 database plus the Python-lowered form, so both server folding behaviours match, and a quoted-case difference is covered by lower(proname). MySQL (257-263) matches LOWER(ROUTINE_NAME) IN names with ROUTINE_TYPE='FUNCTION'. A function in a schema the user cannot see in ROUTINES is one the user lacks EXECUTE on and cannot call, so no reachable counterexample. The docstring matches the code.

relations.py:181-188 selects c.relkind, n.nspname, c.relname and EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM pg_catalog.pg_inherits i WHERE i.inhrelid = c.oid) as the fourth column (row[3], read at line 194). In PostgreSQL pg_inherits, inhrelid is the OID of the child table and inhparent the parent. Every partition or inheritance child, including a sub-partition of a partition, has its own row with itself as inhrelid, so the EXISTS is true at any depth. psycopg2 casts the PostgreSQL boolean type (OID 16) to Python bool, and line 195 checks isinstance(is_child, bool). Based on documented PostgreSQL and psycopg2 behavior plus reading the code; I did not run it against a database. The listed rejection concerns the MySQL routine lookup test and does not cover this claim.

relations.py:193 reads row[3] only inside `if kind in _BASE_TABLE_KINDS['postgres']` (frozenset {'r','p'}, line 52). Non-bool flag raises TypeError (195-200), which is not RlsError so verify_base_tables' `except Exception` (138-155) logs and raises sanitized RlsError 'row-level security could not verify ...; query blocked'. Other relkinds: 'v'/'m' hit _VIEW_KINDS (45-47) and are refused at 228-231 (except allowlisted metadata views, skipped at 191-192); 'f' and None are not in _BASE_TABLE_KINDS so 232-235 raises RlsError 'could not verify a base table'. The flag is never read for those kinds. The rejection line is about a different subject (MySQL routine test), so it does not cover this item.

relations.py:142-155 picks 'relation types or function calls' for postgres/mysql and 'relation types' otherwise, logs 'row-level-security check of %s raised an unexpected %s; failing closed', and raises 'row-level security could not verify {checked}; query blocked'. Grep of the head view for the old message and log text ('could not verify relation types', 'relation check raised an unexpected') finds only: docs/internal/database-connectors/row-level-security.md:47, which already uses the new wording for both cases; tests/unit/test_rls_views.py matches at 147, 282, 394, 540, 552, 657 that use pytest.raises match='could not verify relation types', a regex search that still matches the new postgres/mysql text as a prefix; line 642 expecting the new 'or function calls' text for postgres/mysql; and line 666, which anchors 'relation types; query blocked$' only for sqlite and still matches. The log test at line 278 checks only 'RuntimeError' in the message, so it is unaffected. No other test, doc or caller quotes the old log line 'relation check raised an unexpected'. The rejection line does not concern this claim. I did not run the tests.

RlsGuardRunner.run_sql (safety/__init__.py:167-201) computes rewritten = apply_rls(...) and calls inner.run_sql(args.model_copy(update={'sql': rewritten}), context, require_base_tables=True) when rules exist. ReadOnlyGuardRunner forwards args unchanged (lines 118-119). PostgresRunner.run_sql (postgres/sql_runner.py:168-180) and MySQLRunner.run_sql (mysql/sql_runner.py:137-148) call verify_base_tables(conn, args.sql, dialect=...) and then execute the same args.sql, so the checked text is the rewritten text that runs. The rejection line concerns a different subject (routine lookup test) and is not relied on.

relations.py:123-155: verify_base_tables runs _relations (line 124, sqlglot.parse_one at line 62) and _called_names (line 125, parser_dialect.tokenize at line 96) inside a try, before connection.cursor() at line 128. `except RlsError: raise` (136) is followed by `except Exception` (138), which logs and raises the sanitized RlsError (153-155). RlsError is `class RlsError(Exception)` (rls.py:70), so it is not a base of sqlglot's errors. sqlglot's TokenError and ParseError derive from SqlglotError(Exception), not RlsError, so both fall through to the broad handler. The sqlglot source is not in the view, so that class hierarchy comes from my knowledge of sqlglot.errors and was not read here. No cursor is opened on either failure. The rejections line concerns an unrelated test and does not apply.

tests/unit/test_rls_views.py:482-485 builds (entry[0], 'public', name, entry[1]) = (relkind, nspname, relname, child_flag), matching the real select list at src/sqllens/safety/relations.py:182-183 (c.relkind, n.nspname, c.relname, EXISTS(...)). The code reads row[0] as kind, row[1:3] as (nspname, relname), and row[3] as the child flag (lines 190-194). The fake derives name from params[0].split('.')[-1].strip('"'), and the real code passes relation.sql(dialect='postgres') as the only parameter (line 187). The rejection line concerns the routine lookup, not this claim, so it was not applied.

The docstring (tests/unit/test_rls_views.py:457-464) says routines are matched against the lookup's parameters ignoring case, as the lookup's SQL does, and that a match returns the stored name. The fake (lines 488-492) lower-cases both sides, reads params[1] for pg_proc and all params for ROUTINES, and returns the stored name matched[0]. The real SQL (src/sqllens/safety/relations.py:252, 261) compares proname = ANY(names) or lower(proname) = ANY(names), and LOWER(ROUTINE_NAME) IN (names). It lower-cases only the stored side. The caller builds names as (text, text.lower(), ascii_lower) at relations.py:105-106 and passes them to _refuse_database_routines at line 133. Because the parameters include the lower-case variant, the end-to-end match ignores case, which is what the fake models. The refusal message formats str(row[0]), the stored name (relations.py:269). Fake and real lookups agree on case-insensitive matching and on returning the stored name. The docstring's wording is slightly loose, since the SQL lower-cases only the stored side and relies on the lower-case parameter variant. The rejection line concerns the selected column, not this claim, so I graded without it.

Unnamed-cursor executes in the run_sql paths with statement_timeout_ms=0, require_base_tables=True: (a) MySQL setup cursor 'SET SESSION TRANSACTION READ ONLY' (mysql/sql_runner.py:124, when read_only) -> fake's startswith('SET ') branch (the postgres runner uses conn.set_session, and its SET statement_timeout at :161 is skipped at timeout 0); (b) verify_base_tables (safety/relations.py:128-135) on connection.cursor(): 'SELECT @@lower_case_table_names' (:167) -> @@lower_case_table_names branch; postgres pg_class/pg_inherits lookup (:181-188) -> 'pg_class' branch; mysql information_schema.TABLES lookup (:218) -> TABLES branch; postgres pg_proc (:248) and mysql information_schema.ROUTINES (:258) -> pg_proc/ROUTINES branch. Branch ordering does not misroute: no query contains an earlier branch's marker (pg_proc query has pg_catalog.pg_namespace, not pg_class; ROUTINES query lacks information_schema.TABLES). Everything else hits the final raise AssertionError (test_rls_views.py:493-494). SQLite-only PRAGMA queries are not postgres/mysql runner paths. The query itself (args.sql) runs on a cursor created with args/kwargs, which test helper _catalog_connections (:686-687) routes to a separate recording cursor, not the fake. Rejection line (MySQL routine column) concerns a different defect; not relied on.

tests/unit/test_rls_views.py:686-687 returns query_cursor when args or kwargs are given, else the catalog. Test (tests/unit/test_rls_views.py:722-726) clears routines, runs 'SELECT count(*) FROM orders' on a fresh connection (conns[-1]) and asserts query_cursor.execute.assert_called_once_with(sql). _catalog_connections returns query_cursor only for cursors created with args/kwargs. RlsGuardRunner.run_sql (src/sqllens/safety/__init__.py:196-197) calls _refuse_denied_functions when rules are non-empty, independent of any inner ReadOnlyGuardRunner; it calls assert_no_denied_functions (readonly.py:565) and re-raises UnsafeSqlError as 'refusing to execute SQL: <msg>'. The msg (readonly.py:559-562) is "function 'x' is not allowed: ... refused by the read-only guard's function denylist", which contains 'refused by the read-only guard'. Denylists: sqlite has load_extension (readonly.py:279); postgres set (280-) contains pg_sleep (354); mysql set (394) contains 'sleep' (396); generate_series is in _ALWAYS_DENIED_FUNCS (416-418), merged into each dialect's set (423-426) and matched via sql_names() for typed nodes. The test (tests/unit/test_rls_views.py:757-768) uses a _RecordingRunner inner (no read-only guard) and asserts the match and no inner calls. I did not execute the tests. The rewrite step precedes the denylist and appears to pass these simple SELECTs through unchanged.

src/sqllens/safety/__init__.py:48 imports assert_no_denied_functions into the sqllens.safety module namespace; _refuse_denied_functions (line 204-219), called from RlsGuardRunner.run_sql at line 197 when rules are non-empty, looks it up as a module global at call time (line 207). So monkeypatch.setattr(safety, 'assert_no_denied_functions', boom) in tests/unit/test_rls_views.py:810 replaces what is called. A RuntimeError is not UnsafeSqlError, so it reaches the generic except (line 210) and is raised as UnsafeSqlError('refusing to execute SQL: function denylist check errored (RuntimeError: synthetic)'), which matches the test's regex 'denylist check errored'. The test uses _RULE so self._rules is truthy; inner.calls == [] holds as the raise precedes the inner call. The rejection line concerns a different subject (MySQL routine lookup) and does not apply.

Second half confirmed: apply_rls returns `sql` unchanged when `not rules` (rls.py:219-220), and RlsGuardRunner skips the denylist when rules is empty (safety/__init__.py:196-197), so 'SELECT pg_sleep(1)' reaches the inner runner as-is (test at tests/unit/test_rls_views.py:797-801). First half not settled by reading: with a rule on orders, apply_rls does not short-circuit for unreferenced tables. It parses, runs traverse_scope, and returns tree.sql(dialect=dialect) (rls.py:332), a sqlglot re-render. The inner runner therefore receives the original text only if sqlglot's postgres generator happens to reproduce 'WITH d AS (DELETE FROM public_values RETURNING id) SELECT id FROM d' exactly. Nothing in the code guarantees that. I also cannot confirm that traverse_scope accepts a DELETE CTE without raising. I had no way to execute sqlglot or the test (command not run: pytest tests/unit/test_rls_views.py::test_denylist_check_adds_no_select_only_checks). The rejection line concerns the MySQL routine lookup and does not cover this claim.

relations.py:84-107 _called_names collects any token whose text.upper() is in the dialect tokenizer KEYWORDS and is followed by L_PAREN. sqlglot tokens.py:267 has "AS": TokenType.ALIAS in KEYWORDS, so the 'AS (' in 'WITH "Ä" AS (SELECT 1 AS id) SELECT * FROM "Ä"' is collected (the other 'AS id' is not before a paren). relations.py:61-81 _relations uses traverse_scope, where the CTE reference resolves to a CTE scope source and not an exp.Table, so relations is empty; verify_base_tables (123-135) therefore skips _verify_relations (no pg_class/relation query) and runs only _refuse_database_routines, whose postgres query contains pg_proc (248-254). The test (rls_views.py:271-275) asserts exactly one execute call containing pg_proc, which matches the comment. Not executed, traced by reading. The rejection line concerns a different subject (MySQL routine column).

The 30.x half is confirmed: installed sqlglot 30.26.0 generators/postgres.py:416 has `exp.StrPosition: lambda self, e: strposition_sql(self, e, func_name="POSITION")`. The 25.x half (STRPOS) could not be verified: pyproject.toml:44 pins sqlglot>=25.0,<31, but no sqlglot 25.x source exists in any searched environment (found only 30.26.0, 30.27.0 and two 3.0.x copies), and I did not run a 25.x install. The test (tests/unit/test_rls_views.py:624-628) only asserts membership in {position, strpos}, so it does not settle which name 25.x emits. Missing evidence: sqlglot 25.x dialects/postgres.py StrPosition handling or a run of apply_rls on 25.x.

Installed sqlglot 30.26.0 (.venv) tokens.py:381 has Tokenizer.KEYWORDS "REPLACE": TokenType.REPLACE; the postgres dialect file has no REPLACE mention (no override/removal), so postgres inherits it. Other pinned-range copies (30.2.x) also show the entry (tokens.py:364/378). TokenType.REPLACE is neither VAR nor IDENTIFIER, matching the test assertion at tests/unit/test_rls_views.py:602-603. The pin is sqlglot>=25.0,<31 (pyproject.toml:44); I read only the 30.x copies, not 25-29, but REPLACE has long been a CREATE OR REPLACE keyword so the lower end is very likely the same.

PostgreSQL pg_inherits stores one row (inhrelid, inhparent) per direct inheritance/partition link, for every child regardless of the child's relkind (r, p, f). A grandchild such as orders_2024_q1 has its own row pointing at its direct parent orders_2024, so both are recorded. Absolute-claim input traced: a sub-partitioned child (relkind 'p') and a leaf grandchild (relkind 'r'); src/sqllens/safety/relations.py:183 checks EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_catalog.pg_inherits i WHERE i.inhrelid = c.oid), which matches both. The test at tests/unit/test_rls_views.py:517-526 parametrizes orders_2024 over relkind r/p and uses the grandchild, consistent with the comment. A foreign-table partition (relkind 'f') also gets a pg_inherits row, so the claim holds for it too.

ci.yml:112 sets SQLLENS_TEST_MYSQL_URL=mysql+pymysql://sqllens:sqllens@127.0.0.1:3306/sqllens; urlparse path is '/sqllens', lstrip('/') gives 'sqllens', the database name. factory.py:249 extracts the database for MySQLRunner with the identical expression (parsed.path or '').lstrip('/'), so the test's database matches the connection's. factory.py:203-257 build_sql_runner accepts read_only (default True) and passes it to PostgresRunner and MySQLRunner. With read_only=False, postgres sql_runner.py:145 skips set_session(readonly=True) and MySQL sql_runner.py:118-121 skips SET SESSION TRANSACTION READ ONLY. DDL/DML (CREATE, INSERT, DROP) are not in _READ_SHAPED_KEYWORDS (readonly.py:37-39: SELECT, WITH, UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT, SHOW), so they take the write branch: postgres sql_runner.py:197-200 cursor.execute then conn.commit(); mysql sql_runner.py:153-156 execute then conn.commit(). Each call uses its own connection, so the guarded runner on a separate connection sees the committed objects. The test at test_connectors.py:185-205 uses exactly this runner. Not covered by the supplied rejection, which concerns a different finding.

tests/connectors/test_connectors.py:198-201,221-227: parent has (1,alpha),(2,beta), child inherits with (3,alpha),(4,beta). apply_rls (src/sqllens/safety/rls.py:286-296) appends tenant_id='alpha' to the WHERE of the parent's scan, with no ONLY, so PostgreSQL expands it to the child: rows 1 and 3 survive. count(*)=2, upper(min('alpha'))='ALPHA', strpos('alpha','l')=2. DataFrame built by rows_to_capped_df (src/sqllens/safety/limits.py:70) from dict rows: bigint/int become integer columns and text stays str; .values on mixed dtypes gives an object array, and tolist() yields values equal to [[2,'ALPHA',2]]. The rejection line concerns the MySQL routine-lookup test and does not cover this claim. I did not run the test against a live PostgreSQL.

criteria.json read; criterion 1 present and matches the claim, so judged with siblings. relations.py:181-205: the PostgreSQL relation lookup adds EXISTS(pg_inherits WHERE inhrelid=c.oid); for relkind r/p a True flag raises RlsError('partition and inheritance child tables are not supported ... query the top-level table'); a non-bool flag raises TypeError, which verify_base_tables (138-155) turns into a sanitized RlsError (criterion 6). _relations (61-81) collects every Table source from traverse_scope (top-level FROM, joins, subqueries, CTE bodies) and refuses unaccounted tables. pg_inherits records every child at any depth (a sub-partition is a child of its parent), and the check is rule-independent, so it applies whether or not a rule names the child or parent; the postgres runner calls verify_base_tables before executing (postgres/sql_runner.py:168-169, before cursor.execute at 180). Trigger split: dialect != postgres -> outside the trigger (claim is PostgreSQL only); relkind 'v' metadata-view exemption -> outside the trigger (a view, not a pg_inherits child); lookup exception -> fails closed with RlsError (sibling 6); catalog-qualified/no-row/other-kind -> refused anyway. No departure found. Parent query is allowed: the parent's flag is False, and the rules apply to it. Connector test test_connectors.py:180-230 creates PARTITION OF and INHERITS hierarchies, names the children in rules, asserts child queries raise RlsError 'child tables' (215-217) and parent queries return only scoped rows ([1] for parted; [1,3] for parent, which includes the child's rows). The tests were not run.

criteria.json is a valid list of {criterion,text} and carries criterion 2, so it counts. Read relations.py:84-155,238-270. verify_base_tables is called by the PG/MySQL runners on args.sql (postgres/sql_runner.py:169, mysql/sql_runner.py:138), which is the RlsGuardRunner-rewritten SQL; apply_rls returns tree.sql(dialect) (rls.py:332), so the checked text is the executed text. _called_names (84-107) scans tokens (VAR/IDENTIFIER/keyword before L_PAREN), so typed built-in nodes (strpos, replace) are covered, schema-qualified calls yield the last name before '('. _refuse_database_routines matches proname/lower(proname) against names in pg_proc outside pg_catalog/information_schema across all schemas/signatures (247-255) and LOWER(ROUTINE_NAME) for MySQL FUNCTIONs (257-263). Split conditions: (a) 'not relations and not called' early return (126) -> outside the trigger: fires only when no relation and no call-position name, so no routine call exists; (b) dialect not in (postgres, mysql) -> called=[] -> outside the trigger (SQLite is not in the criterion's PG/MySQL scope); (c) token_type/keyword filter (101-103) -> every call name is a VAR, IDENTIFIER or keyword token, none excluded; (d) lookup exceptions -> caught at 138, fail closed with RlsError (sibling criterion 6). Disputed FAIL (U&"\0066oo"() on PostgreSQL): the tokenizer yields VAR U, AMP, IDENTIFIER, so it parses as a bitwise-and with a call to an identifier named \0066oo; because the check and execution both use the sqlglot re-render (rls.py:332), which emits 'U & "..."()' with spacing, PostgreSQL does not decode a Unicode-escape identifier, and the executed call is to a function literally named \0066oo, which is exactly the name _called_names collects. No check/execute divergence, so the counterexample does not reach a routine call that goes unmatched. I did not run sqlglot; this rests on reading the source and the dispute's own token analysis, which agrees on the parse.

criteria.json is a valid list of {criterion,text}; criterion 3 present, so it counts. src/sqllens/safety/__init__.py:196-197: after apply_rls, `if self._rules: _refuse_denied_functions(rewritten, dialect)` runs irrespective of database.read_only (RlsGuardRunner has no read_only knowledge). _refuse_denied_functions (204-219) calls readonly.assert_no_denied_functions (readonly.py:565-579), which only parses and walks for denied Func nodes (no statement-type/single-statement/DML checks), raising UnsafeSqlError (re-wrapped as UnsafeSqlError 'refusing to execute SQL: ...'; unexpected errors fail closed as UnsafeSqlError). query_database.py:497 surfaces UnsafeSqlError verbatim as with read-only guard refusals. With empty rules the check is skipped (line 196), so unchanged. Split condition `if self._rules`: alternatives -> no rules = outside the trigger (the claim says unchanged there); rules active = check applied. Fault alternative (denylist check raising unexpected exception) fails closed as UnsafeSqlError. Tests in tests/unit/test_rls_views.py: 763-768 blocklisted calls under a rule refused with inner not called (read-only guard not in the stack, i.e. read_only off), 771-776 real read-write runner; 787-794 data-modifying CTE on unprotected table passes to inner unrefused; 797-801 pg_sleep with no rules not refused.

criteria.json read: well-formed list, criterion 6 present and identical to the claim, so it counts. Traced src/sqllens/safety/relations.py (head). verify_base_tables wraps everything in one try (lines 123-135): _relations (sqlglot parse_one/traverse_scope) at 124, _called_names (Dialect.tokenize) at 125, _verify_relations at 131, _refuse_database_routines at 133, cursor creation/close. `except RlsError: raise` (136-137); `except Exception` (138) does logger.warning(..., exc_info=True) (147-152) and raises RlsError('row-level security could not verify {checked}; query blocked') from exc (153-155), with no str(exc) in the message, so no driver detail. Non-bool child flag: lines 193-200 raise TypeError for any non-bool row[3] (including None) on base-table kinds; that is an Exception, so it takes the same sanitized, logged path. Parse/tokenize failures (ParseError/TokenError) are raised inside the try, so they are refused with RlsError.
